# TRF2 Recruits RTEL1 to Telomeres in S Phase to Promote T-Loop Unwinding

The helicase RTEL1 promotes t-loop unwinding and suppresses telomere fragility to maintain the integrity of vertebrate telomeres. An interaction between RTEL1 and PCNA is important to prevent telomere fragility, but how RTEL1 engages with the telomere to promote t-loop unwinding is unclear. Here, we establish that the shelterin protein TRF2 recruits RTEL1 to telomeres in S phase, which is required to prevent catastrophic t-loop processing by structure-specific nucleases. We show that the TRF2-RTEL1 interaction is mediated by a metal-coordinating C4C4 motif in RTEL1, which is compromised by the Hoyeraal-Hreidarsson syndrome (HHS) mutation, RTEL1(R1264H). Conversely, we define a TRF2(I124D) substitution mutation within the TRFH domain of TRF2, which eliminates RTEL1 binding and phenocopies the RTEL1(R1264H) mutation, giving rise to aberrant t-loop excision, telomere length heterogeneity, and loss of the telomere as a circle. These results implicate TRF2 in the recruitment of RTEL1 to facilitate t-loop disassembly at telomeres in S phase.

Cytokines fundamentally control memory T-cell differentiation. Tracking CD8+ T cells from activation to memory, γc-family cytokines IL-7 and IL-15 act at every immune-response stage to promote proliferation and survival, sustaining a stable, long-lived protective memory pool. Separately, CD4+3− inducer cells associate with medullary thymic epithelial cells (mTECs); their RANKL signals drive maturation of RANK-expressing CD80−Aire− mTEC progenitors into CD80+Aire+ mTECs, and RANK-deficient thymic stroma transplanted into immunodeficient hosts induces autoimmunity, revealing a role for CD4+3−RANKL+ cells in intrathymic self-tolerance. Finally, CXCR3, CXCR4 and CXCR7 crosstalk via shared ligands CXCL11 (I-TAC) and CXCL12 (SDF-1). CXCR4 is overexpressed in most human solid tumors and drives metastasis; CXCL12–CXCR4 inhibitors are in preclinical/clinical development, but CXCR7's high-affinity CXCL12 and CXCL11 binding challenges selective CXCR4 blockade.

Three mouse genetic models were reported. mGluR6 knockout mice, exploiting the receptor's retinal ON bipolar cell-restricted expression, lost ON light responses while OFF responses were unchanged; retinal organization and optic fiber projections remained normal, and mutants retained visual behavior in shuttle box avoidance, showing mGluR6 is essential for synaptic transmission to ON bipolar cells and that the OFF pathway carries important visual information. A conditional p75(NTR) allele (p75(NTR-FX)) flanking exons 4–6, encoding transmembrane and cytoplasmic domains with loxP sites, was validated by neural crest-specific p75(NTR)/Wnt1-Cre and conventional null mutants; both showed abnormal hind limb reflexes and peripheral neuropathy. Nrg1/ErbB4 signalling cell-autonomously controls cortical GABA interneuron connectivity development, contradicting the prevailing excitatory-synapse view.
